story: At 5:17 on a sunny Sunday in Sumter Oaks, Gary heads home to Gary's House while Donna, Hal, and Rosa stay out on Magnolia Loop, where the street is buzzing with parade planning. Donna pins a tally sheet for theme ideas to the bulletin board and reminds everyone that cart plans go to Architectural Review first. Hal grudgingly gives Gary the go-ahead on his red and blue light idea, provided he files it properly and keeps the flamingos at three, while Rosa pins up her "Magnolia Loop Memorial Hospital" sketch and invites the whole street to dinner.
events: Donna (street bulletin board): Pin up a tally sheet for parade theme ideas and note that cart plans go to Architectural Review first

Rosa (street bulletin board): Pin up my 'Magnolia Loop Memorial Hospital' theme sketch with a note: all cart plans go to Architectural Review first, ornaments stay at three, and everyone's invited to dinner.

gary.thought_process: Rosa gave me the theme: Magnolia Loop Memorial Hospital, four ambulance carts with red and blue lights. I already said I'd have sketches done by tomorrow and Hal would check them, so I shouldn't repeat that. The best move is to head home and start the wiring sketches on paper. My cart stays in the garage until Architectural Review signs off (L-01), and I filed that application at tick 156. Hal has also been clear that no cart changes happen without review, so paper sketches keep everything legal. Getting to work on this is the useful, needed thing I want to be doing.

parameters.content: Heading home to draw up the ambulance cart wiring sketches on paper, nothing touches the cart until review signs off.

donna.thought_process: Everyone's gathered on the Loop and the parade committee is rolling. Rosa has the ambulance theme, Gary is sketching, and Hal has laid out the rules. I already promised to tally theme ideas at the bulletin board, so the next step is to make that real. Hal said no cart changes without review, so I should lock in that the plan goes through Architectural Review. And I haven't forgotten my pickleball goal: I'll rope Gary in at the same time with a practice session after the sketches.

parameters.content: Pin up a tally sheet for parade theme ideas and note that cart plans go to Architectural Review first

hal.thought_process: Everyone is gathered on Magnolia Loop and the parade talk is moving along. Rosa wants four carts as ambulances with red and blue lights, and that's an exterior modification visible from the street, so L-01 applies. Holiday lights under L-04 aren't legal until Thanksgiving, though this might count as a temporary parade decoration. Bandaged flamingos still count toward Donna's three-ornament limit. Gary says he'll have sketches by tomorrow, and I told Rosa I'd inspect and keep it inside the rules. I shouldn't re-argue what I've already said, so I'll give a precise, useful ruling instead. Gary needs to know the requirement before he starts wiring, and I'd rather he file the review request properly than get a violation. I can be a stickler and still help the thing succeed.

parameters.content: Gary, red and blue lights on four carts is an exterior modification, so L-01 says file it with Architectural Review before you wire anything. Do that, keep the flamingos at three, and I'll sign off on your sketches myself.

rosa.thought_process: Everyone has answered my note. Donna is tallying themes, Gary is sketching, and Hal will inspect by the book. No one is waiting on me to repeat the Hospital theme, so pushing it again would just be noise. The street bulletin board is right here, and Donna asked for theme ideas to go up by tomorrow. I'll pin my ambulance sketch and a note that every cart plan goes through Architectural Review first and stays within Hal's rules. That keeps Hal happy, keeps Gary's carts legal, and gets the Loop closer to entering together.

parameters.content: Pin up my 'Magnolia Loop Memorial Hospital' theme sketch with a note: all cart plans go to Architectural Review first, ornaments stay at three, and everyone's invited to dinner.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
